what_its_for: Dipyridamole is a blood thinner that helps prevent blood clots from forming. It is most often used after heart valve replacement surgery to reduce the risk of dangerous clots. When combined with aspirin (Aggrenox), it is used to lower the chance of having a stroke in people who have already had a stroke or a mini-stroke (TIA).
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food or milk may help if it upsets your stomach. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. Do not crush or chew the tablets unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 75 to 100 mg taken four times a day, or as directed by your doctor. If you are taking the combination product with aspirin (Aggrenox), the usual dose is one capsule twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store dipyridamole at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it can increase your risk of bleeding and may make dizziness worse. Be careful with aspirin or other blood-thinning medicines (like ibuprofen, naproxen, or warfarin) unless your doctor has told you to take them together — combining them raises your bleeding risk. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you take this medication before any surgery or procedure. Avoid activities that could cause injury and lead to difficult-to-control bleeding.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: unusual or heavy bleeding (such as bleeding gums, blood in your urine or stool, or cuts that won't stop bleeding); chest pain or fast heartbeat; sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness, or trouble speaking (these could be signs of stroke); severe dizziness or fainting; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also contact your doctor if your dizziness or headaches are bothersome or do not go away.
when_it_works: Dipyridamole starts working in your blood fairly quickly, but its full protective benefit builds up over days to weeks of regular use. You may not feel any different while taking it — that is normal. It is working quietly in the background to help protect you from clots. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and low blood pressure — rise slowly from sitting or lying down to reduce fall risk. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before taking this medication. People with low blood pressure, heart disease, or bleeding disorders should use this medication with extra caution and close medical supervision. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements.
